record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: How does the minimality problem for positive realizations extend from the single-input single-output case to the multi-input multi-output case? In particular, for positive MIMO systems, what conditions characterize the minimal possible order of a positive realization and how does that theory differ from the SISO case?

evidence.quote: Lastly, we mention the MIMO case, which is not a straightforward extension of the SISO case, as for the existence problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear time-invariant system with p inputs and q outputs whose transfer function matrix H(z) is a q×p matrix of strictly proper rational functions with nonnegative impulse-response coefficients (i.e., the Markov parameters H_k satisfying H(z) = Σ_{k≥1} H_k z^{-k} all have nonnegative entries). A positive realization of H(z) is a triple (A, B, C) with A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, B ∈ ℝ^{n×p}, C ∈ ℝ^{q×n}, all entries nonnegative, such that H(z) = C(zI − A)^{-1} B. Its order is n. The minimal positive realization order N_+(H) is the smallest such n.

Problem: Provide a complete characterization of the minimal positive realization order N_+(H) for an arbitrary nonnegative q×p transfer matrix H(z). In particular:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions on H(z) (in terms of its poles, residues, Hankel matrix structure, or associated polyhedral cones) for N_+(H) to equal a prescribed integer n.

(b) Describe how, and in what essential ways, such a characterization differs from the single-input single-output case (p = q = 1), where partial results based on invariant polyhedral cones containing the reachable/observable sets are available.

(c) Determine whether the gap N_+(H) − deg H(z) between the minimal positive order and the McMillan degree can be bounded by a function of (p, q, deg H), and if so, give sharp such bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The minimality problem for positive realizations is widely reported as still open even in the SISO case; in the MIMO case there are no comprehensive theoretical results characterizing the minimal order, only partial constructions of internally positive realizations. Search results indicate that the MIMO extension is not a straightforward generalization of the SISO theory and remains essentially open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: the characterization of minimality for positive systems is still an open problem
status_evidence.claim: Minimality characterization for positive systems is open, including for MIMO.

status_evidence.title: Representation of a Class of MIMO Systems via Internally Positive Realization
status_evidence.snippet: Internal Positive Realization (IPR) of MIMO systems and filters has been formulated with construction methods
status_evidence.claim: Only construction methods, not minimality characterizations, exist for MIMO positive realizations.
